title: News Brief
purpose: A short, multi-source summary of the week’s world, national, local and sports news for coworkers. Each item blends several outlets; every source is linked so you can read the original.
footer: Compiled Nov. 12, 2026 from public web sources, with reports dated through Nov. 12. Market figures are a snapshot, not a live feed. Election results are unofficial until certified, and fast-moving stories may have changed since publication.

items.headline: Iran says no talks with U.S. as Trump says he doesn’t “need a deal”; Vance reportedly weighs direct talks
items.summary: Iranian officials say there are currently no negotiations with the United States. President Trump posted that the U.S. does not need a deal with Iran and said he had directed Vice President JD Vance to focus instead on crime and corruption in Democratic-run cities, while the Wall Street Journal reported Vance is weighing face-to-face talks with a senior Iranian security official. Fox News, citing Ynet, reported a heated Trump–Netanyahu call over whether to resume strikes, and an Iranian official warned Iran would target U.S. bases if the U.S. attacks its Pickaxe Mountain site. The reports conflict with CNN’s Nov. 9 account that the two sides had been quietly negotiating.

items.headline: Russia–Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi end with a prisoner swap; U.S. envoys head to Moscow
items.summary: Russia and Ukraine held two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, their first in nine months. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the first session very productive and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called it constructive and substantive, with much of the discussion on humanitarian issues. The sides agreed to a prisoner exchange that U.S. envoy Jared Kushner called the biggest ever, but no breakthrough was reported and the talks exposed deep splits over Europe’s role, which Putin has ruled out. Kushner and Steve Witkoff were expected to meet Putin in Moscow on Nov. 12 and then Zelenskyy.

items.headline: Hoax bomb threats hit about 30 European flights; fighter jets escort some
items.summary: A second wave of hoax threats in one week disrupted nearly 30 passenger flights on Nov. 5, forcing diversions and emergency landings, with Italian, French, Bulgarian and Croatian jets escorting some aircraft. An Aer Lingus Dublin–Rome flight was diverted to a French air base. No injuries or explosives were reported. No credible claim of responsibility has emerged, though one threat cited by Birmingham Airport named a group called “Men’s State.” Authorities have warned Russia may be stepping up “hybrid” tactics in Europe, but no attribution has been made for these threats.

items.headline: Qatar-brokered US–Iran talks end without a deal as renewed fighting looms
items.summary: Three days of indirect talks led by Qatar ended without a breakthrough in the eight-month US–Iran war, though Tehran said contacts continued and the next move was Washington’s. Iran’s condensed proposal would have the US lift its naval blockade of Iranian ports and Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz, followed by sanctions steps. The US carried out what an official called “defensive” strikes on Iran’s Qeshm island overnight, and US officials warned fighting could resume after the midterms. Qatar said on Nov. 6 that no comprehensive agreement had been reached.

items.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO
items.summary: Nvidia’s board announced Thursday that Huang has resigned as president, CEO and director, effective immediately, after 33 years. Kress becomes interim CEO while the board searches internally and externally for a permanent successor, and longtime board member Harvey Jones becomes its first-ever chair. The exit follows reports of two extramarital affairs, one with an executive that the New York Times, citing anonymous sources, said U.S. intelligence believed was gathering information for Beijing; China called the claim a smear, and Nvidia’s board said Nov. 8 it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. Nvidia shares fell 13–14% at the open before paring losses. President Trump has suggested former Apple CEO Tim Cook as a successor. Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday, Nov. 17; House Republican chairs had requested a closed-door briefing from Huang on Nov. 18.

items.headline: Wall Street recovers most of an early drop as Nvidia and oil swing
items.summary: Stocks steadied Thursday after absorbing the Nvidia plunge and an oil spike. With an hour left in trading, AP reported the S&P 500 down 0.3%, the Dow down 88 points (0.2%) and the Nasdaq down 0.5% after an early 1.6% loss. Broadcom rose about 5% and AMD about 6%, which AP read as investors seeing the AI business spread beyond Nvidia. Brent crude jumped from about $92 to above $94 after a Trump post, then eased to about $93.79, and the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.07% from 4.98% late Tuesday.

items.headline: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate race; Democrats reach 55 seats
items.summary: The Associated Press called the closest Senate race in the country for Colom on Wednesday evening, after more than a week of counting absentee and provisional (affidavit) ballots. He led Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 4,669 votes at the time of the call, and she conceded in a video message. Colom will be Mississippi’s first Black senator since 1881 and the first Democrat to win a Senate seat there since 1982. The win lifts Democrats to 55 Senate seats with Alaska still uncalled.

items.headline: Alaska Senate: Peltola’s lead grows to about 4,000 votes; final count due Nov. 18
items.summary: With roughly 84% of ballots counted, Democrat Mary Peltola leads Sen. Dan Sullivan by about 4,000 first-choice votes: Tuesday night’s update put her ahead 118,926 (49%) to 114,676 (47.2%), and a smaller Wednesday-evening batch showed 121,487 (48.7%) to 117,512 (47.1%). If no candidate tops 50%, ranked-choice tabulation decides the race, and preliminary data analyzed by the Alaska Beacon and Anchorage Daily News suggests her lead would hold. The next major update is expected Friday, a final count Nov. 18 and certification Nov. 25; Sullivan’s campaign says many ballots remain. A Peltola win would make 56 Democratic senators.

items.headline: October inflation runs hotter than expected; Fed hike widely expected in December
items.summary: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% forecast and down from September’s 0.6%; core prices rose 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast. No annual rate was published because the 2025 government shutdown prevented collection of October 2025 prices. The Fed meets Dec. 8–9 and is widely expected to raise rates, and the S&P 500 slipped more than 0.4% in early trading after the report. The next CPI report is due Dec. 10.

items.headline: Democrats win both chambers of Congress; turnout sets a midterm record
items.summary: Democrats retook the House, on pace for their largest majority since 2008, and flipped the Senate, with gains in Kansas, Ohio, North Carolina and surprise wins in Texas and South Carolina. Turnout exceeded 124 million ballots, a midterm record.

items.headline: Post-election Washington: oversight fights take shape
items.summary: Reuters’ running summaries describe Republican losses leaving President Trump facing tougher congressional scrutiny, with Sen. Elizabeth Warren expected to chair the Senate Banking Committee in January and gain subpoena power. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said in a video message he will fight efforts in Congress to impeach him and defended the Iran war. Reuters also reports Democratic Senate gains could hamper the administration’s push to reshape the courts.
items.note: Single wire service (Reuters); other outlets had not been confirmed at time of writing.

items.headline: NC legislature: Democrats hold the House; one close Senate race could decide control
items.summary: Democrats flipped the state House for the first time since 2010, with unofficial totals of about 71 Democrats, 48 Republicans and one unaffiliated member, and gained four Senate seats, ending the GOP’s veto-proof Senate majority and leaving Republicans a 26–24 edge. That edge rests on Sen. Danny Britt (R-Robeson), who led by fewer than 300 votes. If he loses after a recount the Senate would be tied 25–25, with Lt. Gov. Rachel Hunt breaking ties, and at least five House races are also within recount range. County boards, including Cabarrus, canvass results Friday, Nov. 13; recount requests in county-level races are due by 5 p.m. Monday, Nov. 16; the State Board of Elections canvasses Nov. 24.

items.headline: NC voters approve all three constitutional amendments
items.summary: Each amendment passed with roughly 60% support: photo ID for mail-in as well as in-person voting, a permanent 3.5% cap on the state income tax, and authority for the legislature to limit local property-tax increases. The income tax is already scheduled to fall to 3.49% in 2027. Supporters say the measures protect taxpayers and standardize ID rules; critics, including the NC Budget & Tax Center, warn of strain on state and local budgets.

items.headline: Roy Cooper wins North Carolina’s open U.S. Senate seat
items.summary: The former governor defeated Republican Michael Whatley, with the AP calling the race within minutes of polls closing. He becomes the first Democrat elected to the Senate from North Carolina since 2008, succeeds retiring Sen. Thom Tillis, and will serve alongside Sen. Ted Budd starting in January.

items.headline: Cabarrus voters sweep Democrats onto school board, reject $340M bond
items.summary: Democrats won all three contested Cabarrus County Schools board seats in a historically Republican county, trimming the board’s GOP majority to 4–3. Incumbent Pam Escobar kept her seat, joined by Mishell Williams and Courtney Steinberg. Voters defeated, by about two points, a $340 million bond for new schools and repairs in Cabarrus County and Kannapolis City Schools; a separate $60 million Rowan-Cabarrus Community College bond also failed.

items.headline: Georgia takes No. 1 in the second College Football Playoff rankings; Notre Dame jumps to No. 5
items.summary: The committee’s Nov. 10 rankings run Georgia, Utah, Alabama, UCLA (one of two remaining unbeatens) and Notre Dame, with Miami falling to No. 7 after its 31-24 loss at Notre Dame on Saturday. Georgia moved up from No. 2 after a 35-point win at Ole Miss, and Alabama rose after beating LSU. Notre Dame jumped from No. 11 to No. 5. Three more rankings follow, with the final 12-team field set for Sunday, Dec. 6.

items.headline: Panthers fall 26-21 to Denver on a late strip sack; third straight loss, at New Orleans Sunday
items.summary: Bryce Young threw for 276 yards and three touchdowns (to Tommy Tremble, Darren Waller and Tetairoa McMillan) but lost the game when Nik Bonitto stripped him in the final two minutes with Carolina driving. The Panthers (3-5) have dropped three in a row and visit the Saints (3-5) on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. ET. Analysts noted the offense played well overall, and coach Dave Canales called left tackle Rasheed Walker’s game his best of the season.

items.headline: Hurricanes rout Blackhawks 9-2 and sit atop the NHL; next game is in Helsinki
items.summary: Carolina’s 9-2 win tied its franchise record for goals in a game, with 15 different skaters recording points, and followed a 5-3 win at the Islanders on Nov. 5 in which William Carrier scored the go-ahead goal. The Hurricanes were leading the league in the standings as of Nov. 6. They play Seattle in Helsinki, Finland, on Thursday, Nov. 12 at noon ET, and return home Nov. 19 against Montreal.
